explanation: I found nothing in Mathlib that states this result. The theorem says the degree-0 reduced Mayer–Vietoris sequence of singular homology is exact at the biproduct term. Every map in that sequence is defined in the library itself: `twoOpenReducedMayerVietorisFromIntersectionZero`, `twoOpenReducedMayerVietorisFromBiprodZero`, `reducedSingularHomologyZeroToOrdinary` and the unreduced Mayer–Vietoris maps. The proof combines the library's own unreduced Mayer–Vietoris exactness with the augmentation kernel property, so the mathematical content lies in the library's definitions. I grepped Mathlib/AlgebraicTopology for `MayerVietoris` and `reducedSingularHomology` and got no hits. Across all of Mathlib, `MayerVietoris` only appears in sheaf and sheaf-cohomology files (Topology/Sheaves/MayerVietoris, CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/MayerVietoris, CategoryTheory/Sites/MayerVietorisSquare). None of these covers singular homology.
